chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Sahl, from some of his companions, from al-Ḥasan al-Jahm, who said:

I said to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام: I pass through the market and buy a leather sock, and I do not know whether it is from a duly slaughtered animal or not. He said: “Pray in it.” I said: And the sandal? He said: “It is the same.” I said: I feel constrained about this. He said: “Do you turn away from us? Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام used to do it.”

key_terms.أَتَرْغَبُ عَنَّا: do you turn away from our way or practice
key_terms.أَذَكِيٌّ: from an animal properly slaughtered according to the law
key_terms.السُّوقَ: the marketplace where goods are bought and sold
key_terms.خُفًّا: a leather sock or soft leather footwear

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray in leather footwear bought from the market if its slaughter status is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning praying in footwear bought from the market when one does not know whether the leather came from a duly slaughtered animal. Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام permits praying in such items and reinforces the ruling by referring to the practice of Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام.
